RE-PROP-017.explanation: A section has 640 acres, so 640 / 4 = 160 acres for the SW 1/4, and 160 / 4 = 40 acres for the NE 1/4 of it. The 160-acre answer stops at the quarter section. The rectangular survey is on the national portion even though Georgia uses its own land lot and land district system, plus metes and bounds and recorded plats.

RE-CON-026.explanation: Under O.C.G.A. 10-6A-12 a Georgia broker may act as a dual agent only with the written consent of all clients, and the consent must state, among other things, that the client does not have to consent. Telling only the seller leaves the buyer unaware of the divided loyalty.

RE-CON-027.explanation: In designated agency the broker assigns separate affiliated licensees to each client within the same firm, and O.C.G.A. 10-6A-13(b) provides that the broker is then not a dual agent. Subagency involves a cooperating licensee working for the seller through the listing broker.

RE-CON-028.explanation: A transaction broker assists the parties with ministerial acts without representing any of them as a client; Georgia defines the role in O.C.G.A. 10-6A-3(14). A dual agent does represent both parties, with their written consent.

RE-CON-037.explanation: Under O.C.G.A. 10-6A-5(b) a Georgia seller's broker must disclose known adverse material facts about the property's physical condition that a reasonably diligent inspection would not reveal, whatever the seller says. Waiting for a buyer to ask is not enough.

RE-CON-039.explanation: A seller's broker owes a customer honesty and timely disclosure of known adverse material facts, such as hidden physical defects (O.C.G.A. 10-6A-5(b)). Georgia's statute goes further than common law: O.C.G.A. 10-6A-4(a) says a broker owes no fiduciary duties to any party, client or customer.

RE-DISC-018.explanation: A stigmatized property carries a psychological impact from an event such as a crime or death, not a physical flaw. In Georgia, O.C.G.A. 44-1-16 bars any claim for failing to disclose a homicide on the property, though a direct question must be answered truthfully; a latent defect is a hidden physical problem.

RE-OWN-020.explanation: A special warranty deed, usually called a limited warranty deed in Georgia, covers only defects arising during the grantor's ownership. A general warranty deed gives the broadest protection, covering defects from any earlier owner.

excluded.RE-FIN-001: Deed of trust with a trustee's sale; Georgia home loans are secured by a security deed (deed to secure debt), O.C.G.A. 44-14-60, covered by REGA-GAFIN-001.
excluded.RE-FIN-003: Lien-theory mortgage; Georgia is a title-theory state where the security deed passes title to the lender (O.C.G.A. 44-14-60), so the item would mislead.
excluded.RE-OWN-004: Community property; Georgia is not a community property state.
excluded.RE-OWN-003: Tenancy by the entirety; not a Georgia form of co-ownership, and the national outline does not list it.
excluded.RE-PRAC-009: Computes a broker's fee under a net listing; GREC Rule 520-1-.06(1)(c) prohibits net brokerage engagements, covered by REGA-GACND-001.
excluded.RE-PRAC-002: Says deposit deadlines vary by state; covered by the Georgia items REGA-GAPRC-002 (Rule 520-1-.08(1)(b), O.C.G.A. 43-40-25(b)(23)).
excluded.RE-CON-022: Keys holding disputed earnest money until the parties agree or a court decides; GREC Rule 520-1-.08(3)(b)7 also lets a Georgia broker disburse on a reasonable interpretation of the contract, so the key is not exclusive in Georgia (REGA-GAPRC-003).
excluded.RE-CON-035: Keys keeping the seller's bottom price confidential as a fiduciary duty; under O.C.G.A. 10-6A-5(a)(5) the Georgia confidentiality duty attaches to information the client expressly asks to keep confidential, and 10-6A-4 removes fiduciary status.
excluded.RE-CON-036: Defines a fiduciary duty of accounting; O.C.G.A. 10-6A-4(a) says a Georgia broker owes no fiduciary duties (the duty to account exists as a statutory duty instead).
excluded.RE-CON-040: Says disclosure timing varies by state; Georgia fixes written disclosure no later than the first offer (GREC Rule 520-1-.06(4)(b)), covered by REGA-GAPRC-001.
excluded.RE-OWN-021: Adverse possession tacking with a hypothetical 12-year period; Georgia's periods are 20 years, or 7 under color of title (O.C.G.A. 44-5-163, 44-5-164), covered by REGA-GACLS-006, and the stated 12 years would confuse.
excluded.RE-MATH-016: Transfer tax at a hypothetical $1.10 per $500; Georgia's rate is set by O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 and is tested by REGA-GAFIN-006.
excluded.RE-MATH-015: Proration with the seller owning the closing day as a stated convention; left out so the form does not assert a convention for Georgia contracts.
